To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of fuzzy relevance vector machines (FRVMs) can improve classification accuracy of unbalanced datasets.

(1) the fuzzy membership function can be applied to RVM to improve its generalization performance in learning from unbalanced dataset and noise data; (2) the proposed FRVM is effective in dealing both unbalanced data and noisy data; (3) the proposed FRVMS can be used to select the most important variables from a large number of variables in a high dimension dataset.

(1) the fuzzy relevance vector machine is a novel method to handle unbalanced data and noisy data in machine learning; and (2) the performance of fuzzy relevance vector is comparable with that of SVM, and it is more robust to noisy data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a model from unbalanced data, which is an important issue in many real world applications.
the problem of learning from unbalanced and noisy data using fuzzy membership functions.
the development and implementation of a new approach to the analysis of unbalanced data sets in a classification framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RVM is a very promising tool for the analysis of data with many fewer data points than variables.
the proposed fuzzy relevance vector machine can be used to learn the unbalanced data and reduce the effect of noise.

the RVM is a very good tool for regression and classification, but it has a tendency to over-fit, which can be overcome by the use of a cross-validation procedure, or by using a Bayesian prior on the model parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a fuzzy RVM framework for dealing with unbalanced training data and noise.
FRVM is a promising method for handling unbalanced data and noisy data.
the fuzzy relevance vector machine is an extension of relevance vector machine, and can handle the problems of unbalanced data and noises.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show the importance of the data distribution and the importance of using an appropriate loss function for learning.
the fuzzy relevance vector machine is an effective tool for dealing with unbalanced and noisy data, and it can also provide an insight into the learning process of RVM.
we have developed a new method for learning a fuzzy relevance vector machine that is capable of handling unbalanced data and noisy data.
